Alex Chen: Quick sync - legal pushed back: they need a reproducible evidence package for tenant audits. Not just logs: they want signed assertions that prove which model variant served a request and which key handshake occurred.
Maya Patel: Do we have precedent for 'signed assertions' in exports? Is this a wrapper around logs or a new artifact?
Jordan Lee: Thinking artifact types: (A) raw logs (unchanged), (B) evidence_blob (compact, signed, canonicalized per request), (C) keystore-handshake record (thumbprint + signed token).
Samir Rao: Important: evidence_blob should include request_id, request_headers, model_version, runtime_route (which fallback used), and a signature by our platform signing key.
Luis Gomez: For BYOK customers we must not record plaintext keys. We can store KMS key IDs, wrapped-key thumbprints, and a signed handshake token that asserts key agreement occurred.
Maya Patel: Proposed retention model: hot logs (30 days, full index), mid-term evidence (365 days, indexed by request_id only), long-term legal hold (7+ years, blob store with minimal index).
Jordan Lee: Implementation notes: mid-term evidence should be small (one JSON per request, gzip) and include a verified signature field. Searchability: we keep a tiny index mapping request_id -> blob_path for 365d.
Alex Chen: GA acceptance criteria (minimum):
- export API that returns an evidence package for a tenant/time range
- signed evidence blobs for each request
- keystore-handshake tokens for BYOK tenants
- automated validator that rejects any package containing plaintext keys
- legal sign-off on schema v1
- replay harness & e2e test that reconstructs request ordering
Maya Patel: Can we add a daily canary export job for Dedicated tenants to validate exports end-to-end? Might catch regressions early.
Samir Rao: Yes. Canary export at 00:30 UTC for a small tenant sample. Failure -> alert to eng-ops and block GA promotion for that build.
Luis Gomez: Security control: export pipeline must run inside a restricted job; artifacts should be encrypted at rest and signed. Add an automated scanner that asserts forbidden patterns (PEM headers, private key markers) are absent.
Jordan Lee: Pseudo-check for validator: \n```\nfor file in package_files:\n  assert not contains(/PRIVATE KEY|BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY/)\n  assert evidence_blob.signature is not null\n  assert keystore_thumbprint_format_matches(file)\n```\nMaya Patel: Who owns what? Product owns schema & legal coordination. Eng-runtime + eng-platform implement exporter, signing service, and validator. Security owns validation rules. KMS PM provides wrapped-key-thumbprint endpoint.
Samir Rao: Dependencies list: KMS endpoint (thumbprint) - BLOCKER; infra export pipeline + retention lifecycle; security validation rules; legal schema sign-off.
Alex Chen: Timeline estimate: if KMS endpoint prioritized this sprint we can land alpha (canary) for Dedicated in ~3 weeks, GA in ~10.
Maya Patel: Risks: 1) accidental leakage of key material (mitigate with validator + manual review), 2) legal scope creep (mitigate with schema freeze and explicit acceptance criteria), 3) storage/search cost for mid-term queries (mitigate with compact evidence format + minimal index).
Jordan Lee: UX ask from product: include index.json in package with entries (request_id, timestamp, evidence_blob_path) to accelerate lookups. We'll include it.
Luis Gomez: For legal-hold retention >7y, require human approval workflow and audit trail for enabling/disabling hold. No auto-escalation.
Maya Patel: Action items:\n- Maya: write schema v1 draft by Wed and send to legal\n- Jordan: prototype exporter + package validator by Fri\n- Samir: get KMS PM to commit to API spec and ETA\n- Luis: add forbidden-pattern scanner to export pipeline\n- Alex: schedule legal review session next Tue\nSamir Rao: KMS PM: can deliver wrapped-key-thumbprint endpoint in ~2 weeks if prioritized. I'll coordinate.
Alex Chen: OK. I'll draft a short PRD that captures the acceptance criteria, retention buckets, and risk mitigations, and link it here. Thanks everyone.
Maya Patel: Sounds good. I'll also sketch the export package layout to attach to the PRD.
Jordan Lee: From eng side we're aligned. We'll flag if KMS slips.
Luis Gomez: Adding note: ensure export packages generate a checksum manifest so integrity verification is possible during legal replay.
Maya Patel: Final: prefer immutability for evidence blobs (write-once), and enforce RBAC on export retrieval.
Alex Chen: Closing thread - will post PRD + artifact samples. :thumbsup:
